title: Evolution
tagline: Evidence for evolution, natural and sexual selection, drift, coevolution, speciation, phylogenies, macroevolution and human origins
summary: Nothing in biology makes sense except in the light of evolution, as Theodosius Dobzhansky put it. This course presents the evidence that life has evolved, the processes that change populations — natural and sexual selection, mutation, drift and gene flow — coevolution between species, the origin of species, how phylogenies are read and built, the large-scale patterns of the fossil record, and the evolution of our own species.

chapters.title: Evidence for evolution
chapters.summary: Fossils, homology, biogeography and molecular evidence, and the development of evolutionary thought from Lamarck to Darwin.

chapters.title: Natural selection and adaptation
chapters.summary: Variation, heritability and differential reproduction, and what adaptation can and cannot achieve.

chapters.title: Mutation, drift and gene flow
chapters.summary: The other forces that change allele frequencies, and the neutral theory of molecular evolution in outline.

chapters.title: Sexual selection
chapters.summary: Competition for mates, mate choice and the evolution of differences between the sexes.

chapters.title: Coevolution
chapters.summary: Arms races between hosts and parasites and between predators and prey, and the coevolution of mutualists.

chapters.title: Species and speciation
chapters.summary: Species concepts, reproductive isolation, and allopatric and sympatric speciation.

chapters.title: Phylogenetics: reading the tree of life
chapters.summary: Tree thinking, homology and homoplasy, parsimony and the reconstruction of evolutionary history.

chapters.title: Macroevolution
chapters.summary: Rates of evolution, adaptive radiation, mass extinction and the origin of evolutionary novelties.

chapters.title: Human evolution
chapters.summary: The hominin fossil record, ancient DNA, and the origin and spread of modern humans.
